how: Members recruit contributors around small game figures through direct building proposals.
A defender explicitly says the figure cannot be held alone.
A template invitation receives a bare written acceptance.
Questions about an ongoing canvas discussion receive explanations of the event and its placing rules.
Abandoning an attempt or being unable to finish does not establish personal strain or repair of a quarrel.
Proposing the located chicken project establishes a starter without requiring others to join.
Members propose multiple recognisable figures and one explicitly favours small pictures over a huge logo.
Existing figures attract proposed decorative details and outlines.
Contributors report a starting block and a beak other builders can use.
Reference points, coordinates, and colour directions align contributions during construction.
Already placed beak pixels become a shared instruction for building the rest.
A participant brings a report of chat-based compromise back to the thread without exposing the chat decision process.
A member requests a chat venue for organising helpers without establishing that the request was fulfilled.
Retrospective reports describe members staying awake to repair and protect figures.
A participant explains account-level placement limits and a changing timer without establishing a tested exploit.
Directions and requests for coordination cannot establish organisational nondecision or test the cross-room majority claim.
Opposition to robots and manual repair reports do not determine whether local automation occurred.
A report of chat negotiation does not establish hidden planning or infiltration of rival venues.
Members watch, clear unwanted pixels, restore damage, and report extended defence.
A participant identifies their own mistaken border change and apologises.
Shared border knowledge helps prevent unintended changes, but the revised mechanism of repairing away agreed redesigns remains untested.
Completion thanks receive celebration and renewed defence, returning marking to maintenance.
Expansion and contested space-making within the defence theme cannot all be classified as repair.
Neighbours contact one another, state boundaries, offer concessions, and report agreements.
A member carries negotiation with another group into separate room threads.
Participants yield after a prior-claim request and apologise for unintended border damage.
A neighbour's border complaint receives an offer to trim the figure.
Members locate an initial project, ask where another should go, and consider moving an existing figure.
Occupied prospective space leads participants to cancel a proposed move or wait before building.
Repeated displacement and active opposition lead builders to seek another site.
Leaving an attempt can redirect labour toward a different existing picture rather than move the same design.
Repeated moves return contributors to anchoring and building before they celebrate completion.
Proposed integration does not establish implemented hosting under another room's rules.
Requests, invitations, intended recruitment, and possible credit connect the room to other groups.
A member proposes exchanging defence of existing figures for help maintaining a neighbour's logo.
Proposed barter, attempted recruitment, and possible help retain those evidence states until delivery is demonstrated.
A mutual-defence proposal does not establish a coalition was formed.
Reports explicitly limit agreement coverage to participating placers while destructive or rogue outsiders remain.
A concept quoting another project's handle cannot establish dual membership or divided loyalty.
A request for mutual respect does not establish a developed argument about whether covering art is fair.
Familiar game lore supplies proposed symbols and decorative additions.
Humorous titles turn canvas figures into jokes without demonstrating a sustained running gag.
A neighbour's prior-occupancy claim does not identify a quarrel carried into the event.
Affiliation with another game community does not establish a prior tie selecting an attack target.
Representing an existing community and requesting coordination do not establish a new room forming around a mark.
A humorous figure title alone does not establish an offence dispute or intervention against hate symbols.
Participants explicitly dispute whether an image is an April Fools joke or a fish story.
The local-joke theme includes ordinary game comparison and cannot all be treated as fake news or a coordinated prank.
One member requests a single canvas thread while explicitly disclaiming moderator status.
Annoyance with canvas posts does not establish sabotage of the room's own work.
Canvas activity makes ordinary fanart legible as another placement proposal, changing how members interpret unrelated posts.
Members thank contributors, celebrate survival, and identify their own final pixels.
The final-print post claims a permanent record of the chicken.
Loss and mourning record what happened to figures before the final close as well as in retrospect.
Sharing a media link fits the candidate narrowly without establishing outreach, acknowledgement, or unseen article contents.
An outside representative's offer does not identify a visitor brought to the room by its visible mark.
Survival celebration and a final-print claim do not establish contested versions or correction of the event account.
A permanent final-image claim and a media link do not demonstrate continued organising elsewhere.
Outward pushing and contested boundary-making support limited contention without establishing a coordinated raid.
Unnamed targets and unspecified erased work limit what conflictual space-making can establish about attacks.
The concept quotes only a subreddit handle and cannot establish the contest suggested by its blame label.
An invitation receives a direct report of starting work, supporting the written recruitment-to-building sequence.
The starter's proposal and recruitment call can occupy one turn rather than an observed temporal succession.
A completed figure receives a reply-thread commitment to watch and defend it.
A defender reporting insufficient hands later reports a deal around the same threatened figure, supporting sequence with limited causal warrant.
A border complaint can elicit proposed restraint before an implemented settlement is demonstrated.
Manual repair and incomplete chat visibility cannot determine whether upkeep led to automation.
The completed chicken is celebrated and its contributors thanked.
Recording loss can occur without a preceding celebration of a surviving finished work.
The preserved image and media link do not establish a subsequent decision to continue organising.
A prior-claim request explains one departure without an explicit shortage-of-hands judgment.
A template can accompany an initial invitation while colour alignment continues during building rather than settling earlier debate.
The invitation receives a bare written acceptance while silent responses and the proposed obligation mechanism remain untested.
Defence appeals and promised or possible outside help do not establish delivered assistance caused by insufficient hands.
A barter offer and proposed compromise do not establish later delivery of exchanged help.
Recruitment and later conflict coexist without a passage establishing that one caused the other.
An apology for an unintended border mistake does not establish refusal of a prior attack call.
A border complaint and concession do not establish negotiation as an answer to an attack call.
A narrow quoted handle cannot establish an attack-to-taunting or attack-to-blame sequence.
Intended recruitment of another team's defenders does not establish coalition formation caused by upkeep.
The observed response is a member's complaint while enforcement and recruitment as its cause remain unestablished.
Agreement and limited coverage are reported together, preventing identification of the limit as subsequent rather than concurrent.
